Hierarchical false discovery rate control on a tree

Source: R/share_intervals.R
tree_fdr.Rd

Tests the hypotheses of a tree from the top: the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure is applied within each family of siblings, and the children of a node are tested only when the node is rejected.

Usage

tree_fdr(p, node, parent, q = 0.05)

Arguments

p

Numeric vector of p-values, one per node (NA = not testable; the node and its descendants are not tested).

node

Character vector of node identifiers (unique).

parent

Character vector of parent identifiers; NA, "" or an identifier not in node marks a node of the first family.

q

Target level within each family (default 0.05).

Value

A data.table in the order of node with columns node, parent, p, q_famiglia (BH-adjusted p-value within the family, NA when not tested), tested, rejected.

Details

The procedure follows Yekutieli (2008): the family of the nodes without a parent is tested first with Benjamini-Hochberg at level q; for each rejected node, the family of its children is tested in the same way, and so on down the tree. Yekutieli shows that, with independent p-values, the expected proportion of false discoveries over the whole tree is bounded by q times a factor that depends on the tree (about 2 times the number of levels in the worst case); Benjamini and Bogomolov (2014) give the selective FDR interpretation of the family-wise adjusted values.

References

Yekutieli, D. (2008). Hierarchical false discovery rate-controlling methodology. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 103(481), 309-316.

Benjamini, Y. and Bogomolov, M. (2014). Selective inference on multiple families of hypotheses. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 76(1), 297-318.

Examples

tree_fdr(
  p = c(0.001, 0.4, 0.01, 0.03, 0.2),
  node = c("A", "B", "A1", "A2", "B1"),
  parent = c(NA, NA, "A", "A", "B")
)
#>      node parent     p q_famiglia tested rejected
#>    <char> <char> <num>      <num> <lgcl>   <lgcl>
#> 1:      A   <NA> 0.001      0.002   TRUE     TRUE
#> 2:      B   <NA> 0.400      0.400   TRUE    FALSE
#> 3:     A1      A 0.010      0.020   TRUE     TRUE
#> 4:     A2      A 0.030      0.030   TRUE     TRUE
#> 5:     B1      B 0.200         NA  FALSE    FALSE
